title: Automated Identification, Risk Stratification, and Communication of Incidentally Detected Coronary Artery Disease on CT: CAD-CT Monitor
summary:
This project is a prospective study aiming to improve secondary prevention in patients with incidentally detected coronary artery disease (CAD) on computed tomography (CT) performed during hospitalization at Robert Bosch Hospital. Cardiovascular diseases, and CAD in particular, remain the leading cause of death in Germany.
Coronary artery calcifications can be detected on non-contrast chest CT with high sensitivity and specificity. The identification of coronary artery calcification on CT and the communication of this incidental finding to the treating physician represent an important opportunity to initiate preventive measures at an early stage.
However, in routine clinical practice, information is frequently lost during the detection and reporting of coronary calcification, resulting in inadequate preventive treatment of a substantial number of patients at high cardiovascular risk. This is associated with potentially avoidable cardiovascular events, including stroke and myocardial infarction.
In this project, secondary prevention in high-risk cardiovascular patients will be improved through automated identification of patients with coronary artery calcification, automated risk stratification, and structured communication of the findings to the treating physicians.
